title: It's a great time to be an ADHD game developer
author: cody-fifth-door
selftext:
I have 3 different projects going on right now and I'm making crazy progress on all of them on a given day. One of them is a lieoro inspired game with wizards.   
  
I remember just 3 years ago struggling to get networked destructible terrain working performantly in Godot and I did it in literally 20 minutes with Claude while generating anime girl animations for my other project. 

I love the future.

comments.author: AlienHeadwars
comments.body: It's amazing. Now you can abandon 10 partially completed projects in the time you used to only be able to do 1 or 2.

replies.author: SweetKarmaz
replies.body: Yep! I thought it was odd that OP said they only had 3 projects in development. I have almost 15, and im working on all 15 every week - some more than others. When I get to a point where I can tell the project is not fun (for me) or worth it (as a player), I just leave it, and start another one. So far, 7 have stayed in my current 15, and many others have fallen to the wayside.

replies.author: cody-fifth-door
replies.body:
I intended to actually finish these 3 games not abandon them lmao

I have a bunch of other projects going on too, like using Claude to make shorts content for said games, working on a couple sites, etc.

replies.author: SweetKarmaz
replies.body: Awesome! When you get to a point you want people to test em, let us know!

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body:
I mean you just compost the ideas and repurpose the stuff you made for something else

You've gotta have a recycling system or else you're going nowhere as a creative of any kind

Can't believe people are seriously approaching projects as discrete entities that either finish or are a complete unsalvageable failure.  What an expensive way to make things

replies.author: AlienHeadwars
replies.body: The value salvaged can be through experience and skills, even if a project itself has not produced any component reusable.

comments.author: griminald
comments.body:
Side note: Not unheard of for ADHD professionals to deliberately work on 2+ major projects at a time. 

Nothing motivates an ADHDer to work on Project B quite like procrastinating tasks on Project A.

replies.body: Damn i think i should give that a try haha

comments.author: erratic_ostrich
comments.body:
I don't know if I have ADHD but I totally get that feeling.

The other day I had one AI working on my day job, another working on my game and I was masturbating and getting stoned while I waited for them to finish... it felt so surreal, suddenly programming got so easy that I don't even need to stay sober to work.

What a time to be alive!

On the other hand, I do feel greater pressure to get wealthy asap (hopefuly from a successful game) because this obviously won't last forever and I became too lazy to get a normal job

replies.author: Both_Lawfulness6708
replies.body:
I definitely get the pressure to get wealthy quick.

I feel like we are in a comparative time to the early internet days.

Most people don't really get how AI can help them.

Those that get it, many are not very good at doing it yet.

When I show people what I made I think this is how people felt when showing friends that they ordered a package online to be delivered to the house felt, or built an online store 30 years ago.

comments.author: EC36339
comments.body: I don't know about ADHD, but it's also a great time to be a would be game developer with a 9-5 job.

comments.author: Both_Lawfulness6708
comments.body:
Omg, I think the same thing all the time.

I too have 3 projects.

1 primary, two demos that I'm basically tweaking the visuals on.

I work on them 

1. When I feel inspired about that particular game.

2. The primary game is mechanic heavy strategy game, so mostly in Claude. The other two were written in Claude, so mostly have been tinkering with art in Grok when I run out of Claude or want to save Claude for the strategy game.

And I also have an unfinished survival game.

Claude helps me keep things organized and work on what I want when I want to.
